After a U.S. Navy frigate nearly sank hitting an Iranian mine in the Persian Gulf, American forces launched this 1988 one-day retaliatory strike on Iranian naval targets — what was it called?
Operation Praying Mantis: 1988 US attack on Iran in the Iran-Iraq War.
Known for championing charter schools, this former superintendent led school districts in Philadelphia and Chicago before running — and narrowly losing — a bid for Chicago mayor in 2023. Who is he?
Paul Vallas: American politician and school administrator (born 1953)
Born Saloth Sâr, this Maoist dictator led the Khmer Rouge to power in 1975, presiding over a genocide that killed roughly a quarter of his country's population. Who is he?
As second son and designated heir apparent to Iraq's dictator from 2000, this security official ran the Republican Guard and reportedly authorized torture against dissidents — who was he?

Hitler called him 'the man with the iron heart' — this chief of the Reich Security Main Office and principal architect of the Holocaust was also Deputy Reich-Protector of Bohemia and Moravia. Who was he?
Reinhard Heydrich: German high-ranking Nazi official (1904–1942)

A Russian oligarch who once governed the remote Chukotka region and grew rich through Yeltsin's loans-for-shares scheme, he became famous in England as the former owner of Chelsea Football Club. Who is he?
Born into the Dinka and a rebel fighter from the age of 15, he became the first president of the world's newest nation when it gained independence in July 2011 — who is he?
Salva Kiir: President of South Sudan since 2011.

Touched off by the staged 1931 Mukden incident and the puppet state of Manchukuo, this 1937–1945 conflict — China's largest war of the 20th century — is often called the start of World War II in Asia. What was it?
Second Sino-Japanese War: 1937–1945 conflict in East Asia. It is often regarded as the beginning of World War II in Asia, as the wars became heavily intertwined after Japan's entry into World War II.

Known as 'The Destroyer' within the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu, this deity is the Supreme Lord who creates, protects, and transforms the universe in one major tradition. Who is this god?
Shiva: Major deity in Hinduism. Shiva is one of the five equivalent deities in Panchayatana puja of the Smarta tradition of Hinduism.
A Thracian gladiator born near the Strymon river, this figure led an escaped-slave uprising against the Roman Republic known as the Third Servile War — who was he?
Spartacus: Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt. Spartacus is described to be born near the Strymon river, in Thrace (now known as Bulgaria), possibly from the Maedi tribe.
Born to a Cossack family in Poltava, this journalist-turned-revolutionary became Supreme Commander of the Ukrainian People's Army during the Ukrainian War of Independence — who was he?
Serving as Dachau's second commandant and later the first inspector of Nazi concentration camps, this SS commander was killed in 1943 when his plane was shot down over Kharkov — who was he?
Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
This Japanese term describes marginalized, often homeless youth — a mix of runaways and those seeking community after bullying — who gather in Kabukicho's back alleys. What is this subculture called?
Toyoko kids: Youth group in Tokyo, Japan.
Meaning 'conclusion of the Vedas,' this orthodox school of Hindu philosophy interprets three core texts known as the Prasthanatrayi — what's it called?
Vedanta: One of the six orthodox traditions of Hindu philosophy.
The youngest member of China's Gang of Four, this politician organized the Shanghai People's Commune before being deposed and sentenced to life imprisonment after Mao's death — who is he?
Wang Hongwen: Chinese politician and activist (1935–1992)
A South Carolina Army National Guard officer who served as first gentleman of South Carolina from 2011 to 2017, he is the husband of a former state governor and UN ambassador—who is he?
William Michael Haley: American businessman and officer (born 1970)

Founded in 2012 by former TV journalist Yair Lapid, this centrist Israeli party placed second with 19 Knesset seats in its debut election and later co-founded the short-lived Blue and White alliance in 2019 — which party?
Yesh Atid: Israeli political party. Yesh Atid (Hebrew: יֵשׁ עָתִיד, lit. 'There is a Future') is a centrist political party in Israel.
Atatürk's right-hand man took his very surname from the site of two battles he commanded — and went on to serve as Turkey's president from 1938 to 1950. Which leader earned a name from a battlefield?
Who among these was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year was Janet Yellen born?
Janet Yellen: Yellen is the Eugene E. and Catherine M.
In what year was Hippocrates born?
Hippocrates is also widely recognized for his contributions to medical ethics, being credited with the Hippocratic Oath that remains in use today.
In what year was Zakir Naik born?
Zakir Naik: Zakir Abdul Karim Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
In what year did Guglielmo Marconi die?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year did Ibn Khaldun die?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 – 17 March 1406, 732–808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
In what year was Phosphorus discovered?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

Sukhoi Su-57: Komsomolsk-on-Amur Aircraft Production Association. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Who is credited with discovering Pictor?
Pictor: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pictor is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere, located between the star Canopus and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Who is credited with discovering Proxima Centauri?
Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The first woman to officially attend a Dutch university, she became one of the Netherlands' earliest female physicians and, in 1882, opened the world's first birth control clinic — who was this suffrage leader?
Aletta Jacobs (Dutch; 9 February 1854 - 10 August 1929) was a Dutch physician and women's suffrage activist.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.
Founder of a prominent Russian design studio and an avid, famously foul-mouthed blogger, this designer and entrepreneur is also a member of the Tolstoy family — name this designer?
Artemy Lebedev (born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Composed mostly of plasma along with red cells, white cells, and platelets, this body fluid ferries oxygen and nutrients to cells while hauling waste away — name the fluid?

Blood is a body fluid in the circulatory system of humans and other vertebrates that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells of the body, and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.
The only living group in its tribe, this genus of over 250 fuzzy bees forms small colonies under a single queen — and unlike honeybees, its females can sting again and again — what is it?
Bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.

This quaternary ammonium compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production, and is concentrated in heart and skeletal muscle, though most people synthesize enough on their own. What is it called?
Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
Often preceded by a gallbladder attack and typically caused by a gallstone lodging in the cystic duct, which condition can progress to complications like gallstone pancreatitis?
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. Often gallbladder attacks (biliary colic) precede acute cholecystitis.
Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.
A bright yellow polyphenol found in turmeric, a member of the ginger family, this compound is sold as an herbal supplement, cosmetic ingredient, food flavoring, and food coloring — which compound?
Curcumin is a bright yellow chemical produced by the plant species Curcuma longa.

Occurring five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys,' this linguistic term describes two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, contrasting with a single steady vowel sound — what is it?
Diphthong (DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Discovered to have two undescribed relatives only in 2019, this Amazonian 'knifefish' is best known for generating powerful electric discharges — which species?
Electrophorus electricus is the best-known species of electric eel. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Encompassing everything from oral tales and proverbs to festival rituals and traditional building styles, what term describes the shared expressive culture of a group?
Folklore is the body of expressive culture shared by a particular group of people, culture or subculture.
Ordained a priest in 1923, this Belgian physicist connected an expanding universe to Einstein's field equations and floated an early Big Bang hypothesis — who was he?
Georges Lemaître (lə-MET-rə; 17 July 1894 - 20 June 1966) was a Belgian Catholic priest, theoretical physicist, and mathematician who made major contributions to cosmology and astrophysics.

This small, hardy aquarium fish native to northeast South America gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs, and now ranks among the world's most widely kept tropical species — what fish is it?
Guppy (Poecilia reticulata), also known as the millionfish or rainbow fish, is a member of the family Poeciliidae and, akin to most New World members of the family, is classified as a livebearer.
This field studies the methods historians use — their sources, techniques, and theoretical approaches — in turning the past into an academic discipline — what's this field of study called?
Historiography is the study of the methods used by historians in developing history as an academic discipline.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women as a physical illness in the 19th century, this term for ungovernable emotional excess later became the focus of research by Freud and Charcot — what is this condition called?
Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

This English independent scientist invented the electron capture detector, was first to spot CFCs spread through the atmosphere, and proposed that the Earth behaves as one self-regulating system. Who was he?
James Lovelock (26 July 1919 - 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.
Also known as Al-Kashi's theorem, which trigonometry rule relates the lengths of a triangle's three sides to the cosine of one of its angles?

Law of cosines (also known as the cosine formula or cosine rule or Al-Kashi's theorem) relates the lengths of the sides of a triangle to the cosine of one of its angles. The law of cosines is useful for solving a triangle when all three sides or two sides and their included angle are given.
Descended from the YF-22 prototype, this supersonic air-superiority stealth fighter saw Boeing build its wings and aft fuselage while the prime contractor handled final assembly — what is it?
Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, jet-powered, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft.

This psychiatric state of abnormally elevated energy and mood is sometimes called the mirror image of depression, though its heightened feelings can turn irritable or anxious just as easily as euphoric — what is it called?
Mania (also known as manic syndrome) is a psychiatric behavioral syndrome defined as a state of abnormally elevated arousal, affect, and energy level.
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride salt form as 'crystal meth' — what is it?

Methamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is primarily used as a recreational or performance-enhancing drug and less commonly as a second-line treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
First synthesized in 2003 by Russian and American scientists at Dubna, this synthetic element — atomic number 115 — was named in 2016 for the oblast around its birthplace — what is it?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Found across North America, Europe, North Africa, and Asia, this three-stage amphibian passes through an aquatic larval phase and a land-dwelling 'eft' stage before adulthood — what is it?
Newt is a salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Which applied-math discipline, born from pre-WWII military planning and overlapping heavily with industrial engineering, hunts for the maximum profit or minimum cost in real-world problems?

Operations research (British), often shortened to the initialism OR, is a branch of applied mathematics that deals with the development and application of analytical methods to improve management and decision-making.
Native to the islands of Southeast Asia, this bushy perennial herb in the mint family is prized for a fragrant essential oil used widely in perfumery — what plant is it?
Patchouli (also spelled patchouly or pachouli; Pogostemon cablin) is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, commonly called the mint or deadnettle family.
Its name comes from the Greek for 'love of wisdom,' and physics and psychology were once branches of it — what is this rational inquiry into existence and knowledge?

Philosophy (from Ancient Greek philosophia, lit. 'love of wisdom') is a systematic study of general and fundamental questions concerning topics like existence, knowledge, mind, reason, language, and value.

This category of polymers, most commonly known in the form of PET, is prized for clothing but — unlike some of its naturally occurring plant and insect cousins — rarely biodegrades — what material is it?
Polyester is a category of polymers that contain one or two ester linkages in every repeat unit of their main chain.
Its biological practitioners link it to neuroscience while its social scientists study groups, all in service of studying the mind and behavior — what is this academic discipline?
Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Psychology is an academic discipline of broad scope, crossing the boundaries between the natural and social sciences.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Named after an American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, gram-negative bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes within a single major species — name it?
Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

Drawing on tools from anthropology, biology, medicine, psychology, and criminology, this scientific field studies human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions, distinct from purely social commentary on the subject — what is this field called?
Sexology is the scientific study of human sexuality, including human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions.
This use of the human voice for language ranges from informing and persuading to simply asking or declaring, combining vowels and consonants into meaningful words — what is it called?
Speech is the use of the human voice as a medium for language.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
This vast domain of human practice — divided into visual, literary, and performing branches — lets people transmit values, ideas, and experiences across generations. What is it?
The arts are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
This southwestern European viper's bite can be more dangerous than the common adder's — up to 4% of untreated cases are fatal — which species?
Vipera aspis is a viper species found in southwestern Europe.
Passed only from fathers to sons, this genetic structure carries the SRY gene that typically triggers development of male gonads in mammals — what is it?
Y chromosome is one of two sex chromosomes in therian mammals and other organisms.
Genetic in roughly 80% of cases, this long-term skin condition clogs hair follicles with dead skin and sebum, producing blackheads and pimples on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne: Skin condition characterized by pimples.

German-born theoretical physicist celebrated for E=mc² and work on relativity — he won the 1921 Nobel Prize not for those breakthroughs, but for discovering the photoelectric effect. Who revolutionized physics across multiple domains?
Commonly called buffalo, this large grazing mammal endemic to North America is one of just two living species in its genus, alongside a European cousin — what animal is it?
American bison: Species of bovid artiodactyl mammal.
Known in veterinary medicine as inappetence when it strikes cats, dogs, or cattle, which general medical term describes any loss of appetite — a symptom rather than a diagnosis in itself?
Anorexia (symptom): Loss of appetite. The symptom also occurs in non-human animals, such as cats, dogs, cattle, goats, and sheep.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

Time called her the "literary godmother" to Paris's Lost Generation, and her Black Sun Press printed early Hemingway and Henry Miller — but she also patented the first successful modern bra. Who was she?
Usually arising from damage to the developing brain before birth, this group of childhood movement disorders causes stiff or weak muscles, tremors, and poor coordination — what condition?
Cerebral palsy: Movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)

This ancient insect order traces back to the Late Jurassic, with chewing-mouthpart ancestors called "roachoids" scuttling around some 320 million years ago — yet only about 30 of its 4,600 species ever moved in with us. Which creature is it?
Cockroach: Insects of the order Blattodea.

Used in Chinese medicine for over 1,500 years, this genus of parasitic fungi infects insects and other arthropods, taking its name from Greek and Latin words meaning 'club' and 'head' — which genus is it?
Cordyceps: Genus of fungi. Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Developed as a 14-bed sleeper upgrade of an earlier airliner, which low-wing propeller monoplane cruised at 207 mph and reshaped air travel from the 1930s through World War II?
Douglas DC-3: Airliner and military transport aircraft family.

Defined by permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth and ranging from a 7-inch white-lipped snake to a nearly 19-foot king, which snake family includes most of the world's neck-flaring venomous serpents?
Elapidae: Family of venomous snakes. The family includes 55 genera with around 360 species and over 170 subspecies.

This Irish experimental physicist shared the 1951 Nobel with John Cockcroft for splitting the atom — the first nuclear transmutation, as the prize committee put it, "entirely under human control." Who was he?
Introduced to North America as early as 1840, this large eusocial wasp builds paper-like nests and preys on beetles, other wasps, and dragonflies — which insect is it?
European hornet: Species of wasp. The European hornet (Vespa crabro) is the largest eusocial wasp native to Europe.
Native to the Mediterranean and grown since ancient times, this teardrop-shaped fruit is technically a syconium and comes from the type species of a genus with over 800 members — what fruit is it?
Fig: Species of flowering plant, or its fruit.
This British-American theoretical physicist lent his name to a hypothetical genetically engineered 'tree' and a transform used in additive number theory — who was he?
Freeman Dyson: British theoretical physicist and mathematician (1923–2020)
This mathematician founded set theory and proved that there are more real numbers than natural numbers, revealing an infinity of infinities — who is he?
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Running from your shoulder to your elbow, this long arm bone has a constriction nicknamed the 'surgical neck' due to its tendency to fracture — which bone?
Humerus: Long bone of the upper arm. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections.

Trained originally as a naval architect before becoming a self-taught nuclear physicist, this scientist directed the Soviet Union's atomic bomb program and earned the nickname 'father of the Russian bomb' — who is he?
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Soft, movable, and painless, this benign fatty-tissue growth most often shows up under the skin on the upper back, shoulders, or abdomen — what is it?
Lipoma: Benign tumor made of fat tissue.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.
This American cultural anthropologist's 1928 fieldwork, Coming of Age in Samoa, made her a household name for exploring adolescence and sexuality in Pacific societies — who is she?
Nicknamed a 'semi-lunar' cartilage for its half-moon shape, this crescent-shaped structure cushions joints like the knee, wrist, and jaw — what is it?
Meniscus (anatomy): Fibrocartilaginous part of a bone joint.

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.

Beginning as a tightly compressed gray sponge before expanding into a pitted yellow-brown honeycomb atop a hollow white stem, which springtime fungus is a prized edible found near old orchards and hardwoods?
Morchella esculenta: Species of fungus. The pits are rounded and irregularly arranged.
Originating near the Beijing region and used throughout East Asian cooking, this Brassica rapa vegetable spread to Europe, the Americas, and Australia during the 20th century — which vegetable is it?
Napa cabbage: Subspecies of flowering plant.
Credited with coining the name of a social network that started life as 'Twttr,' this American entrepreneur also co-founded the podcasting company Odeo — who is he?

A subdiscipline of metaphysics, this philosophical study of being asks what reality's most general features are, sorting things into particulars like Socrates and universals like the color green — what is it?
Ontology: Philosophical study of being. For example, social ontology examines basic concepts used in the social sciences.
This cat-family genus contains the five biggest living cats — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — plus extinct relatives like the cave lion and American lion. Which genus is it?
Almost every member of this flightless, countershaded clan sticks to the Southern Hemisphere — except one lone species that creeps up to the equator in the Galapagos. What bird is it?
Penguin: Family of aquatic flightless birds.
With the formula H3PO4, this colorless, odorless compound is typically sold as an 85% aqueous solution and serves as a key ingredient in many fertilizers — what is it?

Its methods range from gentle negotiation and lawmaking all the way to warfare against adversaries, and the social science that studies it tacks 'science' onto its name; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics: Activities associated with group decisions.

Built from long chains of amino acid residues, these biomolecules fold into specific 3D shapes that catalyze reactions, copy DNA, and ferry molecules around the cell. What are these workhorse macromolecules?
Protein: Biomolecule consisting of chains of amino acid residues.
The sole member of its genus and a relative of apples and pears, this hard, aromatic golden fruit is too tart to enjoy raw but turns lovely as jam or a fragrant cheese — what is it?

Marked by tea-colored urine and triggered by crush injuries or extreme exertion, this condition involves skeletal muscle breaking down so fast that released myoglobin can damage the kidneys — what is it called?
Rhabdomyolysis: Condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
This German engineer invented a fuel-efficient combustion engine so influential that both it and the fuel it burns bear his name — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel: German inventor and engineer (1858–1913)
Typically emerging in young adulthood with hallucinations and delusions, this disorder has no objective lab test and needs symptoms for at least six months under the DSM-5 — what is it?
Schizophrenia: Mental disorder with psychotic symptoms.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.
